record.original_question: Construct a Khovanov complex for arbitrary virtual-knot diagrams over the integers, understand the existing constructions that work for large classes of virtual links, and determine structural consequences such as which knots are K-full or Kho-full, whether optimal diagrams are minimal in classical crossing number, and which diagram moves preserve that optimality.

evidence.quote: Construct a generalization of the Khovanov complex for the case of virtual knots that will work for arbitrary virtual diagrams.
The import of our question, is to investigate this structure and to possibly find a way to do Khovanov homology for all virtual knots over the ring of integers.
Are optimal diagrams always minimal with respect to the number of classical crossings?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A virtual knot diagram is a 4-valent plane graph whose vertices are decorated either as classical crossings (with over/under information) or as virtual crossings (drawn with a small circle), considered up to the generalized Reidemeister moves (the classical Reidemeister moves R1, R2, R3 together with the virtual moves V1, V2, V3 and the mixed move M). Khovanov homology, originally defined for classical link diagrams over the ring of integers Z by taking the cube of resolutions of the crossings and applying a (1+1)-dimensional TQFT-like Frobenius structure with appropriately chosen edge signs, gives a bigraded link invariant whose graded Euler characteristic is the Jones polynomial.

Several partial extensions of Khovanov homology to virtual links exist: a Z/2-coefficient theory valid for all virtual diagrams, and Z-coefficient theories defined only for certain classes (e.g. "atomic", orientable, or alternating virtual diagrams) where a coherent sign assignment on the cube of resolutions can be made.

Call a virtual knot K-full (respectively Kho-full) if it admits a diagram on which the Kauffman-bracket-style cube (respectively the Khovanov complex) can be defined over Z in the standard way. Call a virtual diagram optimal if it realizes the minimum number of classical crossings among all diagrams of its virtual knot type.

Solve the following:

(a) Construct a Khovanov chain complex, defined over Z and invariant under the generalized Reidemeister moves, for an arbitrary virtual link diagram, reducing to the classical Khovanov complex on classical diagrams.

(b) Classify all virtual knots that are K-full and all virtual knots that are Kho-full.

(c) Determine whether every optimal virtual diagram of a virtual knot is minimal with respect to the number of classical crossings, and identify which diagrammatic moves preserve optimality.
artifact.status_search_result: Manturov constructed a Khovanov-type complex for virtual knots over arbitrary coefficient rings, and Dye–Kaestner–Kauffman reformulated this to extend Lee homology and a Rasmussen invariant to virtual knots; further work treats alternating virtual links. Thus part (a) has substantial progress, with constructions valid for broad classes of virtual diagrams, but a fully canonical, universally accepted Z-Khovanov theory for all virtual diagrams together with the structural classifications (K-full/Kho-full knots, optimality of diagrams) appears not to be completely settled.

status_evidence.title: Khovanov homology for virtual knots with arbitrary coefficients
status_evidence.snippet: Khovanov homology theory over an arbitrary coefficient ring is extended to the case of virtual knots; a complex is introduced which is well-defined in the virtual case and homotopy equivalent to the original.
status_evidence.claim: Manturov gave a Khovanov complex for virtual knots over arbitrary coefficient rings.

status_evidence.title: Khovanov Homology, Lee Homology and a Rasmussen Invariant for Virtual Knots
status_evidence.snippet: Dye, Kaestner and Kauffman reformulate Manturov's approach and extend Lee homology to the virtual setting.
status_evidence.claim: Further constructions extend Khovanov-type theories to virtual knots, building on Manturov.

status_evidence.title: The Khovanov homology of alternating virtual links
status_evidence.snippet: Khovanov homology for alternating virtual links is studied and computed.
status_evidence.claim: Khovanov homology has been developed for specific classes such as alternating virtual links.
